# strfmt

> String formatting: show(x), cat(...) and fmt("{} and {}", ...) for ints, strings, bools, bytes and slices.

[source](../../registry/strfmt.pkg) · truck

```
use std
use strfmt

let name = "Ada"
let age = 36
print fmt("{} is {} years old", name, age)
print cat("next year: ", age + 1, ", adult: ", age >= 18)
print fmt("|{:-8}|{:6}|", name, age)    // |Ada     |    36|
let xs = make([int], 3)
print cat("xs = ", xs)                  // xs = [0, 0, 0]
```

| package | gives |
|---|---|
| `strfmt/show_int`, `show_str`, `show_bool`, `show_char`, `show_ints`, `show_strs` | `show(x) -> str` for `int`, `str`, `bool`, `u8`, `[int]` and `[str]`; the type of `x` picks the package |
| `strfmt/cat` | `cat(a, b, ...) -> str`: every value shown, one after another |
| `strfmt/fmt` | `fmt(template, values...) -> str`: `{}`, `{:N}`, `{:-N}`, `{:0N}`, `{{`, `}}` |
| `strfmt/lib` | the functions they expand into, and `sf_format(template, vector of strs)` |

`show` packages all start with the same word, and the parser tries each
until the type fits, so `cat` and `fmt` call `show` on each value and
the right conversion is chosen at compile time. Add `show` for your own
types with a package like:

```
syntax expr
  show ( {x: expr ptr Point} ) -> str
expand
  point_str({x})
```

## Packages

| package | summary |
|---|---|
| [strfmt/lib](strfmt/lib.md) | Helper: the functions that strfmt's show, cat and fmt expand into. |
| [strfmt/show_int](strfmt/show_int.md) | show(x) for int: `-42`. |
| [strfmt/show_str](strfmt/show_str.md) | show(x) for str: the string itself. |
| [strfmt/show_bool](strfmt/show_bool.md) | show(x) for bool: `true` or `false`. |
| [strfmt/show_char](strfmt/show_char.md) | show(x) for u8: the byte as a one-character string (`'a'` gives `a`; use `x as int` for its number). |
| [strfmt/show_ints](strfmt/show_ints.md) | show(x) for [int]: `[1, 2, 3]`. |
| [strfmt/show_strs](strfmt/show_strs.md) | show(x) for [str]: `["a", "b"]`, quoted. |
| [strfmt/cat](strfmt/cat.md) | cat(a, b, ...): the values shown as text, one after another. |
| [strfmt/fmt](strfmt/fmt.md) | fmt(template, values...): a template with {} filled in by the values. |
